lemmas.name: ode_wellposed_attractor
lemmas.statement: Globally Lipschitz h gives global existence/uniqueness of ODE solutions; the GAS hypothesis makes {theta*} the unique global attractor.

lemmas.name: conditional_martingale_noise_converges
lemmas.statement: On the event {sup_k ||theta_k|| < inf}, sum_k a_k^2 E[||M_{k+1}||^2 | F_k] <= C sum a_k^2 < inf, so Z_n = sum a_k M_{k+1} is an L2-bounded martingale and converges a.s.

lemmas.name: iterates_bounded
lemmas.statement: Claims sup_n ||theta_n|| < inf a.s. from GAS (Lemma 1) + finite accumulated noise (Lemma 2).
lemmas.note: CIRCULAR: invokes Lemma 2 UNCONDITIONALLY, but Lemma 2 establishes finite noise only on {sup||theta||<inf}, which is exactly this block conclusion. GAS of the ODE does not imply iterate boundedness; the genuine result needs an extra stability hypothesis (Borkar-Meyn: origin GAS for scaled field h_inf), absent here.

lemmas.name: ode_method_convergence
lemmas.statement: A bounded asymptotic pseudotrajectory of theta_dot=h(theta) converges to the global attractor {theta*}.

verdict_reason: Lemma 3 (iterates_bounded) proves boundedness by invoking Lemma 2, whose noise-summability conclusion is itself conditional on the boundedness Lemma 3 is trying to prove. The Lemma2<->Lemma3 dependency is a cycle. Root cause: GAS of the ODE does not imply iterate boundedness/stability; the standard theorem requires an additional stability hypothesis (Borkar-Meyn scaled-ODE h_inf GAS) that the theorem omits and the proof bridges circularly. Audit-only (asymptotic/measure-theoretic; no finite counterexample).

suspects.suspicion: Lemma 2 noise summability holds only on {sup||theta||<inf}; used unconditionally -> circular with Lemma 3
Lemma 3 boundedness hand-waved; GAS of ODE does not imply discrete-iterate stability without extra (Borkar-Meyn h_inf) condition; reuses Lemma 2 which presupposed boundedness
GAS does not make h point inward globally; no Lyapunov/radial condition
Combine inherits boundedness gap; Benaim/Borkar ODE method requires boundedness as input
overgeneralization to all RL algorithms ignores async/biased-noise/divergent FA cases
Picard-Lindelof gives local existence; global needs linear-growth from Lipschitz (minor)
